pr_body:
This PR adds an `/api/v2/data` endpoint to Netdata, offering the following:

- [x] **multi-host** queries
- [x] **multi-context** queries
- [x] **multi-instance** queries
- [x] **multi-dimension** queries
- [x] with **multi-label** filtering
- [x] all "multi" parameters are implemented using simple patterns, to allow pattern matching selections and filtering
- [x] **group by** dimension, instance, node, label are supported, so that the agent aggregates all the data into a small set of result data
- [x] **multiple group by** at the same time. The API supports requesting any combination of group by, including grouping by multiple label keys, all at the same time. So, a user may request group by dimension **AND** label:device **AND** label:type to receive all the combinations of dimensions that match these criteria. Up to 10 label keys can be used in group by statements, which combined to dimension, instance, node give 13 grouping parameters working concurrently.
- [x] when doing multi-context queries that involve metrics with multiple units, another group by parameter is added behind the scenes: `units`. So, the result never mixes apples with oranges. It will return multiple dimensions, one set for each units found in the dataset.
- [x] **group by functions**: average, sum-count, sum, min, max 
- [x] new `jsonwrap` object, providing additional information for the dashboard:
   - [x] ready to use lists for the on-chart drop downs, for nodes, instances, dimensions and labels
   - [x] counters on all of them to show the number of queried metrics per item (per instance, per label, per host, per dimension name)
- [x] this endpoint eliminates completely the need for chart metadata from other sources. So, it includes: units, chart title, dimensions priorities (default sorting), chart type. The only requirement outside this endpoint, is to somehow know the context(s) to query.
- [x] summary statistics are returned for every single item involved (hosts, contexts, instances, dimensions, label keys and label values) to allow the user interface to provide preview of the contribution of each item to the chart.
- [x] api v2 now returns the jsonwrap even if the query does not match any data.

Although most of the code for `/api/v1/data` and `/api/v2/data` is the same, and it has been adapted to support both, `/api/v1/data` should not have any noticeable changes with this PR.

## The problem

Netdata Cloud queries all agents on a per node basis. One query for each node. Also, when a context has many instances (e.g. containers, network interfaces, disks, etc), each agent is sending back an array of values for each dimension queried, which is then aggregated and grouped by Netdata Cloud.

On heavy parents, this is a lot of information to be transferred between agents and cloud.

## The solution

With the changes in this PR, the cloud will be able to ask from the agent to group-by the data the way they are needed for the dashboard, So when for example there are 1000 containers on a node, a context query will only transfer a few dimensions after all the thousands of dimensions have been grouped by the agent.

Also, when working with parents, the cloud could do 1 query for all the nodes the parent hosts. Again, all the dimensions will be grouped by the agent, so that minimum amount of data will be transferred from the agent to the cloud.

This PR will also enable porting the cloud dashboard to the agent.

## group by at the agent

The agent supports 2 kinds of `average`. One is called `average` and it does the obvious, the other is called `sum-count` and return 2 sets of data:

- the sum of the data grouped by
- the count of the dimensions that have been summed

The second can be used by the cloud to calculate the average when doing multi-node queries.

## Other improvements

- [x] a couple of memory leaks have been fixed - they were not noticeable because they were using onewayalloc
- [x] the communication between data collection threads and the streaming sender has been improved by eliminating writing data to the internal pipe when the sender already has other data pending (saved half a core when streaming 3M metrics / second)
- [x] fixed a problem with garbage data being returned due to misuse of a flag
---

Fixes: #14570
pr_comments:
@thiagoftsm I think coverity has been confused. The lock is taken to protect `st->alerts.base`, not `z` or `qX`. `z` and all `qX` variables are single threaded. So, I think all these are false positives.

I had everything in one function, but now they are split into multiple functions. So, I think that if you run coverity again with the new code, these alerts most likely they will not show up.
A final update, I ran tests where I requested more than 50000 URLs and I had success for all requests.

Yes, there was a bug in the use of some flags at the agent, and it was returning random garbage data that happened to be in an unitialized memory.

Please try PR #14564 . This PR does not change anything on `/api/v1/data`, but it has this bug fixed.
